answers.question: What is the inspection interval for the shock strut dynamic seals?

answer.answer:
Inspect the dynamic seals of the MLG shock strut for hydraulic leakage every 500 FH [S1].
Inspect the dynamic seals of the MLG shock strut for hydraulic leakage every 400 FH until the new seal kit is installed [S4].

sources.title: AMM 32-11 - MLG Shock Strut
sources.excerpt:
3.2 Dynamic seal inspection
Inspect the dynamic seals of the MLG shock strut for hydraulic leakage every 500 FH.
The maximum permissible leakage rate at the dynamic seal is 2 drops per minute with the shock
strut compressed. Replace the seals if the leakage rate is more than this limit.
Record the task, the measured values and the date in the aircraft maintenance records. Any value
outside the limits given in this section must be reported to the operator engineering department.

sources.title: SB 32-014 - MLG Shock Strut Dynamic Seal
sources.excerpt:
1 PLANNING INFORMATION
Subject: Main landing gear - Shock strut dynamic seal - Inspection and replacement.
Reason: Operators reported premature wear of the MLG shock strut dynamic seals on aircraft
operated from short runways with a high number of landings.
Compliance: Recommended. This service bulletin applies to all AD-200 aircraft in service.

sources.title: AMM 32-11 - MLG Shock Strut
sources.section: 2.1 Nitrogen charging of the shock strut
sources.excerpt:
2.1 Nitrogen charging of the shock strut
Charge the MLG shock strut with dry nitrogen to a pressure of 1,450 psi at an ambient temperature
of 20 °C, with the shock strut fully extended.
Correct the charging pressure for temperature with the servicing chart: add 4 psi for each degree
above 20 °C.
Do not use compressed air or oxygen to charge the shock strut.

sources.title: SB 32-014 - MLG Shock Strut Dynamic Seal
sources.excerpt:
2.1 Repetitive inspection
Inspect the dynamic seals of the MLG shock strut for hydraulic leakage every 400 FH until the new
seal kit is installed.
If the leakage rate is more than 2 drops per minute, replace the dynamic seals before further flight.

sources.title: SB 32-014 - MLG Shock Strut Dynamic Seal
sources.excerpt:
2.2 Seal replacement
Replace the dynamic seals with the improved seal kit P/N 32-1175-02. After installation of the
improved seal kit, the repetitive inspection of paragraph 2.1 is no longer necessary.
Tighten the shock strut gland nut to a torque of 90 N.m after the seal replacement.
Record the task, the measured values and the date in the aircraft maintenance records. Any value
outside the limits given in this section must be reported to the operator engineering department.
AD-200 Service Bulletin 32-014 - 10 Jun 2025 - SB 32-014 - MLG Shock Strut Dynamic Seal

sources.title: AMM 32-11 - MLG Shock Strut
sources.excerpt:

This chapter gives the servicing and inspection data for the main landing gear (MLG) shock strut of
the AD-200 aircraft. The shock strut is an oleo-pneumatic unit filled with hydraulic fluid and dry
nitrogen.
This revision B applies to all AD-200 aircraft in service. Revision B introduces reduced inspection
intervals following in-service experience, a new gland nut torque value and a new corrosion
inspection of the lower bearing.
Make sure that the safety pins are installed on the landing gear before any task. Put warning
notices in the flight compartment to tell persons not to operate the landing gear controls. Wear
protective goggles and gloves when working with pressurized gas or hydraulic fluid.

answers.question: What is the maximum permissible pitting depth on the chrome surface?

answer.answer: The maximum permissible pitting depth on the chrome surface is 0.25 mm [S1].

sources.title: AMM 32-11 - MLG Shock Strut
sources.excerpt:
3.1 Chrome surface inspection
Inspect the exposed chrome surface of the sliding tube for pitting, scratches and corrosion every 12
months.
The maximum permissible pitting depth on the chrome surface is 0.25 mm. Replace the sliding tube
if the pitting depth is more than this limit.
Lift the aircraft on jacks in accordance with the jacking procedure before the task. Make sure that
the aircraft is in the static ground attitude and that the wheels are clear of the ground. Clean the
external surfaces of the component with a lint-free cloth before the inspection.

strut compressed. Replace the seals if the leakage rate is more than this limit.
Record the task, the measured values and the date in the aircraft maintenance records. Any value
outside the limits given in this section must be reported to the operator engineering department.

sources.excerpt:

sources.title: AMM 32-11 - MLG Shock Strut
sources.section: 2.1 Nitrogen charging of the shock strut
sources.excerpt:
2.1 Nitrogen charging of the shock strut
Charge the MLG shock strut with dry nitrogen to a pressure of 1,450 psi at an ambient temperature
of 20 °C, with the shock strut fully extended.
Correct the charging pressure for temperature with the servicing chart: add 4 psi for each degree
above 20 °C.
Do not use compressed air or oxygen to charge the shock strut.

3.1 Chrome surface inspection
Inspect the exposed chrome surface of the sliding tube for pitting, scratches and corrosion every 12
months.
The maximum permissible pitting depth on the chrome surface is 0.25 mm. Replace the sliding tube
if the pitting depth is more than this limit.
Lift the aircraft on jacks in accordance with the jacking procedure before the task. Make sure that
the aircraft is in the static ground attitude and that the wheels are clear of the ground. Clean the
external surfaces of the component with a lint-free cloth before the inspection.
